question: Combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs) reduce clinical hyperandrogenism in PCOS and idiopathic hirsutism by suppressing LH-driven ovarian androgen production and simultaneously increasing sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), which lowers free androgen levels.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. COCPs work via two mechanisms: (1) progestogen suppresses pituitary LH, reducing ovarian thecal androgen production; and (2) the oestrogen component increases hepatic SHBG synthesis, lowering free testosterone levels. Both mechanisms contribute to the reduction of hirsutism and acne.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. COCPs act by a dual mechanism: the progestogen suppresses LH (reducing thecal androgen synthesis) and the oestrogen component stimulates hepatic SHBG production, reducing bioavailable free testosterone. This dual effect makes COCPs effective first-line medical therapy for androgen-related symptoms.
